claims.text: As-processed refractory high-entropy alloys have a relatively uniform, coarse-grained microstructure.
The uniform, coarse-grained baseline provides high strength.
The uniform, coarse-grained baseline exhibits pronounced impact-induced energy release.
The uniform, coarse-grained baseline has limited ductility and nonuniform deformation.
The proposed intervention is controlled deformation followed by partial recrystallization to create a gradient or bimodal grain-size distribution.
Controlled deformation and partial recrystallization can produce the proposed hierarchical grain-size distribution in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Grain-size gradients are among the microstructural approaches investigated for improving strength-ductility synergy in high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys.
A gradient or bimodal grain-size distribution will improve ductility and uniform deformability in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed gradient microstructure will preserve the alloy's high yield and ultimate strength.
The proposed gradient microstructure will preserve impact-induced energy release.
Fine-grained surface or interfacial regions promote localized plasticity.
Fine-grained regions may activate deformation twinning.
Plasticity and possible twinning in the fine-grained regions delay macroscopic strain localization.
Coarse-grained domains retain the alloy's high strength.
Coarse-grained domains retain the alloy's impact-energy-release capacity.
Spatial grain-size variation decouples the conventional ductility-strength trade-off.
Refractory high-entropy alloys are intended primarily for high-temperature structural applications.
The predicted improvement will hold under dynamic, elevated-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions typical of energetic structural applications.
